notes: Medium polyglot/low-level pipeline chaining five independent subsystems into one /app/solve.py whose generated /app/answer.json and /app/recreate.vim must be consistent with independently-recomputed behavior. The wasm part requires selecting a WebAssembly runtime (Node.js WebAssembly API driven from Python via subprocess), invoking the exported probe() and reading linear memory at the returned offset; malformed/missing binaries must raise ValueError. The higher-order part demands mutable-closure shared state, currying (incl. variadic), and mutual recursion, all handling negatives/zero. The object part requires a value-derived __hash__ consistent with __eq__ (the shipped buggy_point.py shows the identity-hash failure mode). The iteration part consumes the constant only by importing compute_seq and reading .ITERATIONS dynamically (a hidden test overrides the constant and requires the work length to follow it; hardcoding 731 fails a source grep). The Vim part must emit canonical tab/split commands that replay to the exact 2-tab/3-buffer topology in a fresh vim -u NONE (source + separate inspector, reproduced for a freshly re-emitted script). Hidden cases cover closure/negative/zero edges, value-hash collisions, malformed and missing wasm inputs, and an iteration-constant override. Difficulty comes mostly from dependent_stages + hidden_case_generalization + adversarial_inputs + tool_breadth (range 10-17, medium).
